does the number of interface change runtime? If not why don't you cache the interfaces on first time fetch?

But getInterfaces() is called only once during Manager object creation at service startup. So i believe caching is not needed because there’s only a single call anyway.
Any thoughts?
what does this mean? The neighbour is added by default without detecting any? What does neighbour mean here?
I have changed the name to interfaces and yes, once the active interfaces are fetched by getInterfaces(), the dbus object will be created for each interface.
Done
making the property as readonly in yaml does not fix this?

The properties under the "receive" object are meant to be readonly, as they represent information received from neighbors and are updated automatically by the lldp service. Users cannot modify these.

But the properties under the transmit object are writable/configurable at runtime, since they define what this device advertises to neighbors.

So probably making it read-only or writable cannot be possible, as long as we provide explicit methods to write tlvs for transmit object I guess. (I will discuss this in the dbus interfaces commit review).

For now, this commit chain will focus on the receive objects only. Runtime LLDP configuration of the transmit object can be a future work item.
if object path does not chage in runtime, make it static?

The base object path is already defined as a static constexpr in LLDPManager, as it does not change at runtime.

Each Interface object has a different object path (/xyz/openbmc_project/network/lldp/<ifname>), so this member does change per instance. So it cannot be static, I believe.
Can we move this out of constructor and do the interface fetching asynchronies. This can improve the startup time of service.
Done
